content: Your duty is to be, and not to be this or that. 'I am that I am' sums up the whole truth; the method is summed up in 'be still.'
author: Ramana Maharshi
sourceWork: Talks with Sri Ramana Maharshi, Vol. 2
explanation:
Human suffering is born of ceaselessly attaching adjectives and identities to the pure sense of existence: I am successful, I am a failure, I am anxious, I am unloved. Ramana Maharshi cuts through all psychological clutter to the primordial core of awareness: before you became a role, a profession, or a story, you simply ARE. When you cease superimposing temporary labels on consciousness, you discover the unbroken peace that has always been present.

Stillness is not an achievement or a rigid discipline; it is the natural state of awareness when the restless mind stops chasing thoughts.
practicalInsight: Whenever you feel overwhelmed today, pause for three breaths, drop all your roles and titles, and simply rest in the pure, quiet sense of 'I AM.'
reflectionPrompt: Who are you when you strip away your job title, your history, your anxieties, and your possessions?
